sections.html:
Joliet is the Will County seat, about 40 miles southwest of Chicago, and a small part of the city lies in Kendall County. Population was 150,362 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 152,241 for 2025. The city reaches into nine townships: Joliet, Plainfield, Troy, New Lenox, Jackson, Channahon and Lockport in Will County, and Na-Au-Say and Seward in Kendall County.

That patchwork has a practical result. Your address may sit in a different school district, assessor's office and tax bill from a neighbor a few blocks away, so check the parcel before assuming anything. Locals speak of an east side and a west side relative to the Des Plaines River, plus a far west side that includes the Kendall County land.

For 2020 to 2024, 73.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with a median home value of $265,800 and 51,055 households. Median gross rent is $1,276. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,960, compared with $819 for owners with no mortgage. About 26.3 percent of homes are not owner-occupied, so landlords and tenants figure in many Joliet sales, and with 28.8 percent of residents speaking another language at home, bilingual paperwork can be useful.

Joliet was settled in 1833 and reincorporated as a city in 1852. During the 1930s many owners could not keep up their large houses, and in the 1940s big Victorian homes were divided to house several families. Absentee landlords and deferred maintenance followed, and heavy use of vinyl siding changed several historic limestone buildings. The Joliet East Side Historic District, created in 1980, and the Upper Bluff Historic District, created in 1991, are both listed on the federal historic register.

  • If your house stands in one of those districts, ask the city's Planning and Zoning staff what review applies before you plan repairs.
  • If a large older house was ever split into units, bring any records of that conversion.
  • Buyers of pre-war houses commonly ask about foundations and wiring, so have repair records ready.

Joliet has moved from a steel and manufacturing town to a commuter city. I-80 and I-55 meet near Channahon, and US 6, US 30, US 52 and US 66 also cross the city, as do Illinois Routes 7, 53, 59 and 171. The Joliet Transportation Center is the final stop for the Metra Heritage Corridor and Rock Island District lines, and Amtrak stops at Joliet Union Station. Pace buses leave a downtown terminal about once an hour, six days a week. The mean commute is 28.8 minutes.

Schools vary by address. Joliet Public School District 86 and several smaller districts feed Joliet Township High School District 204. Other parts of the city fall in Plainfield District 202, New Lenox District 122 and, in Kendall County, Minooka and Oswego districts.

sections.h2: City requirements before a house sells
sections.html:
The seller of residential or commercial property inside city limits buys the transfer tax stamp. The city prints the cost as $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price. The stamp applies only to incorporated Joliet, and the city offers an address verification map and a phone line for borderline addresses.

  • A completed water and lien letter must reach the city at least four business days before closing. Forms received later may not be processed before the closing date.
  • An exempt stamp, with no charge, is needed on any deed change inside city limits, such as adding or removing a name, moving a property into or out of a trust, or a divorce.
  • Exempt stamps require the original signed and notarized deed, not a copy, with exempt language on it or a completed city exemption form.
  • Start or stop water service through Customer Service at 815-724-3820, option 2.

Questions about stamps go to the Customer Service real estate transfer stamps desk at 815-724-3902. Most exterior projects, including fences, decks, pools, patios, garages, additions and concrete work, need a building permit and a plat of survey, so look for those before you list.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Will County
sections.html:
The Will County Recorder of Deeds is at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, phone 815-740-4637. The fee schedule effective October 1, 2025 lists $90.00 for a standard document and $118.00 for a non-standard one. A standard document stays within up to five property index number references and up to five related document references.

A deed needs a notarized original deed, grantee name and address, a tax bill-to name and address, a property address, a permanent index number, the real estate transfer tax declaration or exemption, and the municipal transfer tax stamp. Joliet is one of nine Will County municipalities that require that stamp.

Charge or stepCost or deadlineOffice
City transfer stamp$3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price, bought by the sellerCity of Joliet
Water and lien letterReceived at least four business days before closingCity of Joliet
Exempt stampNo charge, original deed requiredCity of Joliet
Standard document recording$90.00Will County Recorder
Non-standard document recording$118.00Will County Recorder

The state tax comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Ask the title company for the county portion and the total due at closing.

Will County owners call the Will County Treasurer's Office or the Supervisor of Assessments for tax bills, homestead exemptions and appeals. Kendall County owners call the Kendall County Treasurer and Assessment Office. The back of your property tax bill lists your township assessor's contact.

If the house is a rental, the city runs a Rental Inspection Program with an owner registration form, a landlord checklist and a fee schedule. Ask Neighborhood Services at 815-724-4090 whether the property is registered before you tell a buyer anything about it.

The city also bans parking on streets automatically when 2 inches or more of snow falls within 24 hours, under City Code Sec. 19-142, and prohibits boats, RVs, trailers and trucks over 8,000 pounds on streets and in residential parkways. Buyers who own a trailer or boat will ask about both.

Each step waits on the one before it, so work backward from the closing date.

  1. Check the address verification map to confirm the parcel is in incorporated Joliet, and note whether it is in Will or Kendall County.
  2. Get the original deed signed and notarized, with exempt language if the transfer is exempt.
  3. Send the completed water and lien letter to the city at least four business days before closing.
  4. Buy the stamp before recording.
  5. Record the deed with the Will County Recorder of Deeds, or through the Kendall County offices for a parcel there.

Missing any one of these can push a closing back. If you are moving out, call Customer Service about stopping water service.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell a Joliet house fast?
sections.html:
Each option suits a different situation.

  • List with an agent. A house in good repair does well on the open market.
  • Sell on your own. You handle the contract, the city stamp and the water and lien letter yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer. It can fit an inherited house, a rental with tenants or a property with a failed inspection, and closing can follow the schedule you need.

A cash sale has no lender appraisal to wait on, so the city paperwork above is usually what sets the pace.

faqs.q: What is the population of Joliet, IL?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 152,241 residents. The 2020 census counted 150,362.

faqs.q: How much is the Joliet transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The city prints $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price, and the seller buys the stamp. Exempt stamps carry no charge.

faqs.q: How early must the water and lien letter reach the City of Joliet?
faqs.a: At least four business days before closing. Forms received later than that may not be processed before the closing date.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Joliet house?
faqs.a: Joliet is the Will County seat, so deeds go to the Will County Recorder of Deeds at 158 N. Scott Street. The fee for a standard document is $90.00.

faqs.q: Does a Joliet house in Kendall County use a different office?
faqs.a: Yes. A small part of Joliet is in Kendall County, so that parcel's tax bill and deed run through Kendall County offices. The city's address verification map and the tax bill show which county applies.
